QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r15.claim: Angels carry the soul to God, either to the درجات of ʿIlliyyīn or the درجات of Sijjīn; another image has God clothing, cleansing, and praying over the soul in mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r15.anchor: إما إلى عليين - ثم لها تفاوت درجات ، وإما إلى سجين - ولها تفاوت دركات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r3.claim: Fronting to your Lord makes Him the exclusive destination, and fronting on that day specifies the time of departure from worldly life; the destination is more important, so it comes first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r3.anchor: فإن تقديم {إلى رَبِّكَ} يفيد القصر والاختصاص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r4.claim: Masaq describes the soul's movement at death toward God, followed by the grave, which is only visited; mustaqarr in 75:12 describes the final abode after Resurrection, Paradise or Hell, where the journey ends.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p223/r4.anchor: اختير لفظ (المساق) ههنا لأن الآية في مفارقة الروح الجسد عند الموت

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r10.claim: “Masāq” is a mim-form verbal noun for being driven; the person is seized and compelled to God’s presence for reckoning and recompense.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r10.anchor: “Mesāk” da sevk mânasına mimli masdardır. Yani o gün o kişi yakalanır

ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.claim: For lovers of this world, death is painful and endless separation and exile; for those devoted to the afterlife, the same moment brings release and joyful union.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#5/r11.anchor: bu lahza dünya mahabbetine sargın rûhlar için böyle elîm bir firak, nihâyetsiz bir hicran

NAHHAS:v5p92/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r8.claim: The clause “to your Lord that day is the journey” occupies the position of the answer to idha.

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r1.claim: Al-Masāq is a verbal noun on the pattern of maqāl from qāla yaqūlu, derived from sāqa yasūqu.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r1.anchor: المساق مصدر من ساق يسوق ، كالمقال من قال يقول

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r2.claim: One interpretation is that the Lord is the destination toward which people are driven.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r2.anchor: أن يكون المراد أن المسوق إليه هو الرب

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the Lord is the one driving them that day, with their being driven entrusted to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون المراد أن السائق في ذلك اليوم هو الرب ، أي سوق هؤلاء مفوض إليه

STUDYQURAN:75:30/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r1.claim: Some say this describes God driving the soul out of the body at death.
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r1.anchor: the manner in which God drives the soul from the body at the moment of death

STUDYQURAN:75:30/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r2.claim: Others take it as God driving the soul toward the Final Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r2.anchor: the manner in which God drives the soul toward the Final Judgment

STUDYQURAN:75:30/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r3.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r3.claim: Another reading makes it a challenge: “Who will heal him?”
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r3.anchor: Others say that it is a challenge, meaning, “Who will heal him?”

STUDYQURAN:75:30/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r4.speaker: God
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r4.claim: A hadith qudsī has God say to return His servants to earth, from which they were created, into which they return, and from which they will be brought forth again.
STUDYQURAN:75:30/r4.anchor: where God is reported to say, “Return My servants to the earth, for verily, I have created them from it

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r14.claim: Al-masaq is a verbal noun for being driven; the destination is return to God, and the wording signals no choice or escape from this course beginning at death.

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r15.claim: If the fronted phrase marks exclusivity, the destination is return to God alone.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r15.anchor: ولو كان تقديم { إلى ربك } لإفادة الحصر أفاد انحصار الغاية في الرجوع إليه تعالى

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r16.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r16.claim: One alternative supplies ‘judgment’: the person is driven to God’s judgment for His decision.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r16.anchor: وقيل الكلام على تقدير مضاف وتقديم { إلى ربك } لإفادة الحصر والتقدير إلى حكم ربك يومئذ المساق

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r17.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r17.claim: Another supplies ‘appointment’: the person is driven to the Lord’s appointed destination, Paradise or Hell.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r17.anchor: أو التقدير إلى موعد ربك وهو الجنة والنار

TABATABAI:75:24-30/r18.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r18.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r18.claim: A further interpretation says return to God means God alone is the one who drives the person.
TABATABAI:75:24-30/r18.anchor: وقيل المراد برجوع المساق إليه تعالى أنه تعالى هو السائق لا غير

TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.claim: Al-Qummī says that when the soul reaches the collarbone someone asks who can treat or recite over him; he knows it is separation, and the final journey is to the Lord of the worlds.
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r12.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { كلا إذا بلغت التراقي } قال يعني النفس

TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.claim: In al-Kāfī, Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir, answering Jābir, says the dying person asks for a doctor, realizes he is leaving loved ones, and that one leg entwining with the other is the world entwining with the hereafter; the journey is to the Lord of the worlds.
TABATABAI:75:16-40/r13.anchor: إلى جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { وقيل من راق وظن أنه الفراق }

TABRISI:75:29-36/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:29-36/r8.claim: All creatures are driven to the gathering place, where God alone holds authority to command and forbid.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r8.anchor: مساق الخلائق إلى المحشر الذي لا يملك فيه الأمر والنهي غير الله تعالى

TABRISI:75:29-36/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:29-36/r9.claim: Alternatively, an angel carries the soul where God has commanded, to ʿIlliyyūn for a person of Paradise or Sijjīn for a person of Hell; masāq is the place of driving.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r9.anchor: يسوق الملك بروحه إلى حيث أمر الله تعالى به إن كان من أهل الجنة فإلى عليين وإن كان من أهل النار فإلى سجين

BURSEVI:v10p197/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r6.claim: Every person is driven to God and His judgment, where no one else has authority to rule.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r6.anchor: أي إلى الله وإلى حكمه يساق الإنسان لا إلى غيره أي يساق إلى حيث لا حكم هناك إلا الله

BURSEVI:v10p197/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r7.claim: المساق is a verbal noun of driving, expressed in Persian as being driven.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r7.anchor: فالمساق مصدر ميمي بمعنى السوق بالفارسية راندن

BURSEVI:v10p197/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r8.claim: The definite article in المساق substitutes for a genitive complement, meaning the driving of the human being.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r8.anchor: والألف واللام عوض عن المضاف إليه أي سوق الإنسان

BURSEVI:v10p197/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p197/r9.claim: Kāshifī glosses the destination as the return of everyone to the recompense of their Lord.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r9.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : بسوى جزاى رورد كارتو آروز باز كشت باشد همه كس را

THALABI:v10p90/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p90/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p90/r5.claim: The destination and return are to God; angels drive the soul wherever God commands.
THALABI:v10p90/r5.anchor: إلى ربك يومئذ المساق المنتهى والمرجع تسوق الملائكة روحه حيث أمرهم الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r1.claim: The destination and return are to God, as angels drive the spirit where He commands.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r1.anchor: المنتهى والمرجع بسوق الملائكة الروح إلى حيث أمر الله سبحانه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r4.claim: “The legs become entwined” means the deceased has severed ties with worldly life and is moving toward the afterlife and the divine presence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r4.anchor: “Bacaklar birbirine dolaşır” ifadesi, “Artık ölen kişinin dünya ile ilgisi kesilmiş, âhiret hayatına, ilâhî huzura yönelmiştir” şeklinde açıklanmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r5.claim: The dead can no longer act by their own will; God judges them by their worldly deeds and sends believers to Paradise and disbelievers to Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:26/r5.anchor: Allah katında durumu dünyada yaptıklarına göre değerlendirilir; müminlerden ise cennete, inkârcılardan ise cehenneme gönderilir.

BURHAN:v3p448/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p448/r7.claim: A second type of paronomasia adds letters in one of the paired words, as “the leg” and “the driving” differ by an addition.
BURHAN:v3p448/r7.anchor: وأما بزيادة في إحدى الكلمتين كقوله تعالى ﴿ والتفت الساق بالساق إلى ربك يومئذ المساق ﴾

ITQAN:v3p244/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p244/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p244/r1.claim: Jinās is verbal resemblance; similar sounds draw the listener's attention, and a shared form used first in one sense and then another arouses expectation.
ITQAN:v3p244/r1.anchor: هو تشابه اللفظين في اللفظ قال في كنز البراعة وفائدته الميل إلى الإصغاء إليه فإن مناسبة الألفاظ تحدث ميلا وإصغاء إليها

ITQAN:v3p244/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p244/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p244/r10.claim: Nāqiṣ jinās differs in letter count, with the extra letter at the beginning, middle, or end; examples include sāq/al-masāq and kullī/kulli.
ITQAN:v3p244/r10.anchor: ومنها الناقص بأن يختلف في عدد الحروف سواء كان الحرف المزيد أولا أو وسطا أو آخرا

ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r3.claim: At that point he feels impelled to turn toward his Sustainer.
ASAD-NOTES:75:26/r3.anchor: at that time towards thy Sustainer does he feel impelled to turn

ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r1.claim: The driving toward the Sustainer is belated repentance.
ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r1.anchor: i.e., with belated repentance (see next three verses)

ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r2.claim: The wording rendered “at that time” literally reads “on that day”; the note breaks off while discussing yawm.
ASAD-NOTES:75:26#n12/r2.anchor: "on that day"; but the term yawm is

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r8.claim: Fronted destinations in these return passages express that return and final gathering are to God alone, with no other destination.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r8.anchor: فالمساق إلى الله وحده لا إلى ذات أخرى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r9.claim: Some explain the fronting as matching the verse endings; Samarrāʾ rejects this and says it marks exclusivity.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r9.anchor: وهذا ليس من التقديم من أجل مراعاة المشاكلة لرؤوس الآي كما ذهب بعضهم بل هو لقصد الاختصاص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.claim: He once went home when he wished, but now is driven to his Lord and master against his will.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.anchor: فهو كان يذهب إلى أهله وينقلب إليهم متى شاء، أما الآن فإنه يُساق سوقاً إلى ربه وسيده على الرغم من أَنْفِهِ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.claim: Worldly destinations were open, so the phrase was not fronted; now he is driven like a slave to one Lord, and fronting the destination signals no choice.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.anchor: فليس ثمة حصر، ولذا لم يقدم الجار والمجرور في الدنيا، فقد كانت له فيها الحرية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.claim: The daily trip home needed no date, but his final being driven to the Lord occurs on the appointed day of departure; the contrasting phrases frame opposite scenes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.anchor: فإنه كان في الدنيا يذهب كل يوم وليس في يوم معيّن، أما سوقه إلى ربه فذلك في يوم معين

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r3.claim: No one escapes: all must undergo death's agony and, helplessly, begin the journey toward their Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r2.claim: The death scene warns pleasure-seekers that death will strip away their vigor, the Day of Judgement is certain, and they should prepare to return to God before death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p79/r2.anchor: Those who are slaves to worldly pleasures are reminded of the agonies of death

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r5.claim: The departure to God rebukes a person who pursued worldly luxuries until he lost his strength and asks how he can now reach his Lord in that condition.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r5.anchor: Once the correct meaning of the shank embracing the shank is understood

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r1.claim: المساق is a verbal noun from سوق meaning the return and final destination, either Paradise or Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r1.anchor: إلى ربك يومئذ المساق: المرجع والمصير، والمساق مفعل من السوق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r1.claim: The destination is God and His judgment, with no other destination; an implicit إضافة of حكم is understood, and fronting المساق emphasizes exclusivity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r1.anchor: أي إلى اللهتع إلى وحكمه سوقهلا إلى غيره على أن المساق مصدرميمي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r2.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r2.claim: Alternative explanations take the destination as God’s appointment, meaning Paradise or Hell, or posit that God Himself is the driver and all are driven to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r2.anchor: وقيل هو موعد والمراد به الجنة والناروقيل هناك مضافمقدر على أن الرب جل شأنههو السائق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r3.claim: Whether the passage concerns only the wicked or both wicked and righteous, the driving is suited to each group’s destination.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r4.claim: The verse is glad tidings for those who think well of their Lord and know His mercy precedes His wrath, as the cited hopeful poem illustrates.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية لعمري بشارة لمنحسن ظنه بربه وعلم أنه الرب الذيسبقت رحمته على غضبه قالواغدا نأتي ديار الحمى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r5.claim: The answer to إذ is omitted and supplied from context: events unfold, truth is revealed, or a person finds the good or evil deeds he performed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148/r5.anchor: ثم إن الجواب إذ محذوفدل عليه ما ذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r10.claim: That day the servants are driven back to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r10.anchor: أي مرجع العباد [يومئذ] (2) إلى الله يساقون إليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r7.claim: His legs twist together, leaving him unable to move them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r7.anchor: والتوت ساقه بساقه فلا يقدر على تحريكهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r8.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means the hardship of leaving this life joins the terror of the afterlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r8.anchor: أو شدة فراق الدنيا بشدة خوف الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r9.claim: Al-masāq means the driving, its destination, and its time; all fall under the rule of the Lord who sent and supported the Prophet.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r10.claim: After death angels drive each person toward clear happiness or misery; alternatively, the phrase means presentation before God, where “I will die and rest” cannot help the sinner, who is received like an absconding slave according to his disobedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r10.anchor: فإما أن تسوقه الملائكة إلى سعادة بينة وإما إلى شقاوة بينة

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the procession to the Lord takes place in the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إلى ربك يومئذ المساق} قال: في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r4.claim: The address shifts from the plural audience in ‘you love the immediate life’ because that address is generic and unspecified, making variation apt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r4.anchor: والخطاب في قوله : { إلى ربك } التفات عن طريق خطاب الجماعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r5.claim: The article in المساق is generic, encompassing everyone including the rejecting human; alternatively it replaces a genitive complement, the course of the man who asks when Resurrection will be.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r5.anchor: والتعريف في { المساق } تعريف الجنس الذي يعم الناس كلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r6.claim: المساق is the mimetic verbal noun of ساق, leading someone before oneself toward a destination, opposed to القود; metaphorically it is bringing him to meet his Lord’s recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p359/r6.anchor: و { المساق } : مصدر ميمي ل ( ساق )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.claim: Alternatively, the فاء connects to 75:30: the person has left life and is being taken to God without provisions for that meeting; the context implies his knowledge of loss and regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفاء تفريعا وعطفا على قوله : { إلى ربك يومئذ المساق }

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425/r1.claim: The final destination is to God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r1.claim: The return and destination are to God: the spirit rises to heaven, then God orders it returned to earth, from which humanity was created and will be raised again.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الروح ترفع إلى السماوات، فيقول الله عز وجل: ردوا عبدي إلى الأرض،

JISHUMI:v10p7193/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r23.claim: The person is driven to God's judgment and whatever He decrees for him; this urges obedience and warns against disobedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r23.anchor: يعني يساق إلى حكمه، وما يأمر له فيه، وذلك حث على طاعته

JISHUMI:v10p7193/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r24.claim: Another view says an angel drives the soul to the destination God commands.
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r24.anchor: وقيل: يسوق الملك روحه إلى حيث أمر الله به

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r15.speaker: خارجة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r15.claim: Al-masaq means the departure or onward journey.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r16.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r16.claim: Al-masaq means the final resting place.

MUQATIL:75:22-33/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r9.claim: The final destination in the afterlife is God, from whom there is no departure.
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r9.anchor: يعني النهاية إلى الله في الآخرة ليس عنها مرحل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r1.anchor: هو مصدر ساقه أي مساق العباد إلى حيث أمر الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r2.claim: The servants are driven where God commands, either to Paradise or to Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#7/r2.anchor: مساق العباد إلى حيث أمر الله اما إلى الجنة أو إلى النار

QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r9.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talha transmits Ibn Abbas’s view that the last worldly day meets the first hereafter day, unless God has mercy, as death’s agony meets the encounter’s terror.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r9.anchor: وروى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: { والتفت الساق بالساق } قال: آخر يوم من الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r13.claim: Another view says the disbeliever’s soul is punished as it leaves the body, then comes the resurrection’s hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r13.anchor: وقال قوم: الكافر تعذب روحه عند خروج نفسه، فهذه الساق الأولى

QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r14.claim: Qurtubi glosses the destination as your Creator, that day as the Resurrection, and al-masāq as the return.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r14.anchor: أي إلى خالقك { يومئذ } أي يوم القيامة { المساق } أي المرجع

QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r15.claim: A tafsir says the person is driven to God by the angel who recorded his evil deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r15.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير قال: يسوقه ملكه الذي كان يحفظ عليه السيئات

QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r16.claim: Al-masāq is the verbal noun of sāqa yasūqu, like al-maqāl from qāla yaqūlu.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:29-30/r16.anchor: والمساق: المصدر من ساق يسوق، كالمقال من قال يقول
